intent: Let `app_icons generate --linux-out` emit hicolor PNGs for home_inventory, so its .desktop entry and launcher icon can be regenerated instead of being hand-kept.
scope: python_pkg/app_icons/apps.py — the home_inventory registry entry only
Non-goal: no change to glyphs, palette, sizes or the CLI surface
changes: home_inventory: linux=False -> linux=True. Its desktop app is a Chrome-wrapper around the Flutter web build and ships a .desktop entry + hicolor icon theme, so it genuinely has a Linux target; with the flag false cli.py skipped --linux-out for it silently, emitting nothing and reporting success.
No test change needed: test_cli.py's linux-out test asserts over todo (linux=True) and dufs_client (linux=False), neither of which this touches.

verification.evidence: 43 passed; every app_icons module at 100% line and branch coverage
wrote 6 asset files + 8 hicolor PNGs (16..512); before this change the second line was absent
installed home-inventory.png into ~/.local/share/icons/hicolor and home-inventory.desktop into ~/.local/share/applications

risks: Running `generate --linux-out <dir>` with no --app now also writes home_inventory PNGs into that directory; harmless, since icon_name namespaces the files (home-inventory.png).
The generated PNGs live in the consuming repo, not here, so a palette change there needs a regenerate step in that repo.
rollback: Set linux=False on the home_inventory AppIcon entry and re-run the app_icons test suite.
After rollback, ~/home_inventory/desktop/icons is stale-but-valid: the committed PNGs keep working, only regeneration stops.
